newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines buying state-owned shares.
newsitem.headline: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines buying state-owned shares.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV said Thursday it was buying back state-owned shares worth about one billion guilders ($571.4 million) in a move seen as enhancing its appeal to investors and potential partners.

KLM and the government said in a joint statement they had agreed in principle that KLM would buy back some 17.3 million ordinary shares held by the state, reducing the government's voting stake to 25 percent from the current 38.2 percent.
The shares will subsequently be retired, reducing KLM's capital base and boosting earnings per share by an estimated 20 percent, KLM said.
"We have done a good deal with the government...which gives us the opportunity to privatise further, in line with other European airlines," KLM spokesman Hans Leijte said.
"The deal will bring us closer into line with prevailing market conditions and ... offer us important strategic advantages."

Shattering foreign perceptions of KLM as a state-controlled airline would, for example, stand the carrier in good stead in an upcoming review by U.S authorities of the anti-trust immunity granted to KLM's partnership with Northwest Airlines Corp., Leijte said.
U.S authorities are due to re-evaluate the anti-trust status, granted in 1993, some time next year.
